objects.description: Opaque-like, variable-sized bitmask structure storing a 2D bitmap for pixel-perfect collision. Fields: w (width in pixels), h (height in pixels), and a flexible trailing array bits (declared as size 1, allocated larger) of machine words (BITMASK_W) that hold the bit data column-major by word blocks. Bits are accessed with bitmask_getbit/setbit/clearbit using x,y coordinates. Instances must be created with bitmask_create and freed with bitmask_free due to variable-sized storage.

functions.name: bitmask_create
functions.description: Allocate and return a new bitmask with dimensions w by h. The mask is zero-initialized (all bits cleared). Use to create masks for pixel-perfect collision tests.
requirements: Caller must free the returned mask with bitmask_free() to avoid memory leaks
Returns NULL on allocation failure (not documented here; treat return value as nullable)

functions.name: bitmask_free
functions.description: Release all memory associated with a bitmask created by bitmask_create (or functions that allocate compatible bitmasks such as bitmask_copy/bitmask_scale).
requirements: m must be either NULL or a valid pointer returned by bitmask_create/bitmask_copy/bitmask_scale
Do not use m after calling bitmask_free (pointer becomes invalid)
Do not free the same bitmask more than once

functions.name: bitmask_copy
functions.description: Create and return a deep copy of the given bitmask m. Useful to duplicate masks for modification without affecting the original.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask
Returned pointer must be freed with bitmask_free()
Treat the return value as nullable on allocation failure (not documented here; be defensive)

functions.name: bitmask_clear
functions.description: Clear all bits in the bitmask m (set all bits to 0).
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer

functions.name: bitmask_fill
functions.description: Set all bits in the bitmask m (fill with 1s).
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer

functions.name: bitmask_invert
functions.description: Flip all bits in the bitmask m (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0).
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer

functions.name: bitmask_count
functions.description: Count and return the number of set bits in the bitmask m.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer

functions.name: bitmask_getbit
functions.signature: static INLINE int bitmask_getbit(const bitmask_t *m, int x, int y);
functions.description: Return nonzero if the bit at coordinates (x, y) is set in m; otherwise return 0. Coordinates start at (0,0). Inline for performance.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer
Behavior is undefined (out-of-bounds memory access) if x or y are outside the mask dimensions

functions.name: bitmask_setbit
functions.signature: static INLINE void bitmask_setbit(bitmask_t *m, int x, int y);
functions.description: Set the bit at coordinates (x, y) in m. Inline for performance.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer
Behavior is undefined (out-of-bounds memory access or memory corruption) if x or y are outside the mask dimensions

functions.name: bitmask_clearbit
functions.signature: static INLINE void bitmask_clearbit(bitmask_t *m, int x, int y);
functions.description: Clear the bit at coordinates (x, y) in m. Inline for performance.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask pointer
Behavior is undefined (out-of-bounds memory access or memory corruption) if x or y are outside the mask dimensions

functions.name: bitmask_overlap
functions.signature: int bitmask_overlap(const bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, int xoffset, int yoffset);
functions.description: Test whether two bitmasks a and b overlap (have any common set bits) when b is offset relative to a by (xoffset, yoffset). Returns nonzero if overlapping, 0 otherwise. Offsets may be negative.
requirements: a and b must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive
No modification to inputs

functions.name: bitmask_overlap_pos
functions.signature: int bitmask_overlap_pos(const bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, int xoffset, int yoffset, int *x, int *y);
functions.description: Like bitmask_overlap, but if an overlap exists, write one point of intersection into *x and *y in a’s coordinate space. If there is no overlap, *x and *y are left untouched. Returns nonzero if overlapping.
requirements: a and b must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive
x and y must be valid, writable pointers when the function is called (the function may write to them if an overlap is found)

functions.name: bitmask_overlap_area
functions.signature: int bitmask_overlap_area(const bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, int xoffset, int yoffset);
functions.description: Compute and return the number of overlapping bits (the area of overlap) between bitmasks a and b with b offset by (xoffset, yoffset).
requirements: a and b must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive

functions.name: bitmask_overlap_mask
functions.signature: void bitmask_overlap_mask(const bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, bitmask_t *c, int xoffset, int yoffset);
functions.description: Compute the overlap (bitwise AND under translation) of a and b with b offset by (xoffset, yoffset), and write the result into mask c.
requirements: a, b, and c must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive

c must be pre-allocated and large enough to receive the overlap result; exact required dimensions are not specified here. Typical usage implies c has the same dimensions as a (unknown if strictly required)

functions.name: bitmask_draw
functions.signature: void bitmask_draw(bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, int xoffset, int yoffset);
functions.description: Draw (bitwise OR) mask b onto mask a with b translated by (xoffset, yoffset). Useful for composing larger masks from submasks.
requirements: a and b must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive
Only bits within a’s bounds are affected; ensure a is sized to receive the intended region

functions.name: bitmask_erase
functions.signature: void bitmask_erase(bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, int xoffset, int yoffset);
functions.description: Erase bits in a wherever mask b has bits set when translated by (xoffset, yoffset). Typically implements a = a & ~translated(b).
requirements: a and b must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive
Only bits within a’s bounds are affected; ensure a is sized to cover the intended region

functions.name: bitmask_scale
functions.signature: bitmask_t *bitmask_scale(const bitmask_t *m, int w, int h);
functions.description: Return a new bitmask that is a scaled version of m with dimensions w by h. Scaling quality is reasonable but not guaranteed perfect. If either w or h is 0, a clear 1x1 mask is returned.
requirements: m must be a valid, initialized bitmask
Returned mask must be freed with bitmask_free()
If w == 0 or h == 0, caller should expect a 1x1 clear mask

functions.name: bitmask_convolve
functions.signature: void bitmask_convolve(const bitmask_t *a, const bitmask_t *b, bitmask_t *o, int xoffset, int yoffset);
functions.description: Convolve mask b into mask a and write the result into output mask o, shifted by (xoffset, yoffset). If offset is 0, the output bit (x,y) is set iff bitmask_overlap(a, b, x - b->w - 1, y - b->h - 1) is true. Modifies a rectangular region of o.
requirements: a, b, and o must be valid, initialized bitmasks
xoffset and yoffset can be negative or positive
o must be pre-allocated and large enough to hold the modified region: at least cover x in [xoffset, xoffset + a->w + b->w - 1) and y in [yoffset, yoffset + a->h + b->h - 1) as per the comment
a and b are not modified
